The panic is `parseDays` in `schedule/weekly.go`. It panics on any unrecognized day name, and user input reaches it through `POST /v1/reminders`. The fix should return an error, not panic. I'll check how the caller handles errors and how this code came to be.

The panic is in `parseDays`, which has no error path. `parseWeekly` already returns an error, and the API caller already handles one with a 400. So the fix is to have `parseDays` return an error. Before I write the reproducer, I need the zone helper's signature.

{"title": "schedule.parseDays panics on an unknown day name from user input", "body": "Fingerprint fp_fe620b, 10 reports, all in v1.4.0 (commit 9c41e7a). Panic: "schedule: unknown day <name>", for example "Funday", "tues", "thurs". The requests were POST /v1/reminders with "every":"on <days> at <hh:mm>".

Cause: schedule/weekly.go parseDays panicked on any day token missing from dayNames. Parse -> parseWeekly -> parseDays runs on user input from api.createReminder (api/reminders.go:53), and the panic is not recovered on that path. parseWeekly already returns an error, and the handler already maps errors to 400, so an unknown day should be a 400 error, not a crash.

Fix: parseDays now returns ([]time.Weekday, error). parseWeekly propagates the error. Reproducer: schedule/parse_days_test.go, TestParseUnknownDayIsError. It panicked before the fix and passes after it. The full test suite passes.
